browser-cdp-bridge-spike-hardening.title: Harden ShizukuUserServiceProvider callback lifecycle
browser-cdp-bridge-spike-hardening.description:
Address two High findings carried over from browser-cdp-bridge-spike round 3 review:
1. ServiceConnection callbacks (onServiceConnected/Disconnected/BindingDied/NullBinding) do not verify they belong to the current connection or that the provider is not closed; a stale callback from a prior bind cycle can corrupt state or resume a newer pending obtain(). Add a per-bind generation/connection-identity token and ignore stale callbacks.
2. Failure callbacks (onServiceDisconnected/onBindingDied/onNullBinding) call completeWithError but do not call unbind; failed binds can leak until session shutdown. Clear connection state and call unbindUserService on each terminal failure callback.
3. Add tests for: stale callback after timeout/close (must be ignored), unbind asserted for each failure callback, no race between old callback and new obtain().
acceptCriteria: ServiceConnection callbacks verify connection identity (e.g., generation token) before mutating state
All terminal failure callbacks (disconnect-before-connect, onNullBinding, onBindingDied) call unbindUserService
Tests assert unbind on each failure callback and assert stale callback is ignored after close()
browser-cdp-bridge-spike-hardening.note: DONE — commits 445362ca + ff873f25 merged to main 2026-05-03 12:20. Codex round-2 APPROVE. Single-flight + refcounted awaiters pattern; concurrent obtain() callers share one CompletableDeferred; binder.bind() runs exactly once per cycle; cycle torn down only when last awaiter abandons it. Post-onServiceConnected cancellation atomically clears inflight before completing deferred. 15/15 tests.

browser-script-host-cancel-guard.title: Add cancellation guard to ScriptHostWebViewClient page-load callbacks
browser-script-host-cancel-guard.description:
Address one High finding carried over from browser-script-host round 3 review: ScriptHostWebViewClient has no cancellation guard in onPageFinished or in the evaluateJavascript callback. If timeout/cancellation happens while pageReady.await() is pending, a queued onPageFinished or eval callback can run before cleanup and start arbitrary agent JS. A long script can block the main thread before the drain destroys the WebView.

Fix: have onPageFinished and the prelude-eval callback check the runner's cancelled flag (already wired) BEFORE injecting prelude / evaluating user script. If cancelled, do nothing (cleanup will tear down the WebView). Add a JVM test using a fake WebViewClient adapter that asserts cancellation observed before onPageFinished prevents prelude injection.
acceptCriteria: ScriptHostWebViewClient.onPageFinished checks the cancelled flag before injecting the prelude
Prelude evaluateJavascript callback checks the cancelled flag before evaluating user script
JVM test asserts cancellation prevents prelude injection / user script evaluation

browser-screenshot-artifact-formatting.title: screenshot() helper writes to artifact + returns file path
browser-screenshot-artifact-formatting.description:
Original framing was wrong (intercept Page.captureScreenshot bytes in BrowserScriptBridge — fragile, has to special-case CDP methods, breaks if CDP adds more byte-returning methods). Correct framing: agent-script-layer concern. screenshot() helper in page.js writes the bytes to the trace dir via TraceRecorder.storeBytes (already exists at app/src/main/kotlin/ai/closepaw/trace/TraceRecorder.kt:27, returns TraceArtifactRef with .path) and returns the on-device path instead of base64. Agent gets a path it can adb-pull / hash / hand to follow-up tools, but does not eat 100-500KB base64 in its context window.

Current state:
- app/src/main/assets/agent_skills/browser-use/scripts/page.js screenshot() returns {data: result.data, format, widthCss, ...} — base64 inline.
- app/src/main/kotlin/ai/closepaw/browser/script/BrowserScriptJsInterface.kt only exposes send + done — no artifact API to JS.
- app/src/main/kotlin/ai/closepaw/browser/script/BrowserSessionManager.kt:52 already injects TraceRecorder (currently @Suppress unused).

Implementation:
1. Plumb TraceRecorder through to BrowserScriptJsInterface (add to constructor).
2. Add @JavascriptInterface fun storeArtifact(kind: String, filenameHint: String, base64: String, mimeType: String?): String? that decodes base64, calls traceRecorder.storeBytes(kind, filenameHint, bytes, mimeType, description), returns ref?.path (or null if recorder disabled — JS treats null path as missing).
3. Modify page.js screenshot(): after CDP call, const path = await bridge.storeArtifact(`browser-script`, `screenshot-${Date.now()}.${format}`, result.data, `image/${format}`). Return {path, format, widthCss, heightCss, devicePixelRatio, scale, estimatedBytes}. NO data field.
4. SKILL.md: update screenshot description — `screenshot() returns a path on device, not raw bytes. The trace dir for the current session is also where agent.log lives. Use the path with shell tools if you need to inspect; do not paste bytes into your context.`
5. Tests: BrowserScriptJsInterface unit test for storeArtifact (verify base64 decode + storeBytes called + path returned). page.js doc/example update.
6. Real-device sanity: dispatch ./scripts/debug-run.sh `Take a screenshot of example.com and tell me where you saved it` on nubia or emulator-5556 — verify the agent gets a path, not a base64 blob, in tool output.
acceptCriteria: BrowserScriptJsInterface gains storeArtifact(kind, filenameHint, base64, mimeType) JS-callable method
TraceRecorder plumbed from BrowserSessionManager to BrowserScriptJsInterface (no longer @Suppress unused)
page.js screenshot() returns {path, format, widthCss, heightCss, devicePixelRatio, scale, estimatedBytes} — no data field
SKILL.md screenshot guidance updated to reflect path-not-bytes contract
Unit test asserts: base64 decode + storeBytes called with correct kind/filenameHint/mimeType + returned path matches ref.path
Real-device sanity run on nubia or emulator-5556: agent screenshot returns a path string in tool output (no base64 blob > 1KB visible in agent.log)

browser-cdp-command-timeout-recovery.title: Map CDP command timeouts to JS rejection + broken/recovery decision
browser-cdp-command-timeout-recovery.description: Holistic review High #5: ChromeCdpClient.sendRaw() times out with TimeoutCancellationException, but BrowserScriptBridge.dispatch() rethrows all CancellationException instead of rejecting the specific CDP promise. The script then waits for the global tool timeout; BrowserSessionManager does not mark the CDP connection broken for that path. Map per-command timeouts to a typed CDP error that rejects the JS promise with a recognizable code/name; decide whether the per-command timeout should mark the client broken (probably yes after N consecutive timeouts, configurable). Add tests for promise rejection, trace outcome, and next-call recovery semantics.
acceptCriteria: Per-command CDP timeout rejects the originating JS promise with typed CdpException (not coroutine cancellation)
Repeated/decision-rule timeouts can mark the client broken so next browser_script call reconnects
Tests cover promise rejection, broken transition policy, and next-call recovery
browser-cdp-command-timeout-recovery.note: DONE per KISS — typed CDP timeout error + JS promise rejection both shipped. ChromeCdpClient.kt:199-210 catches TimeoutCancellationException and rethrows as CdpException(-1, `CDP command ... timed out after Nms`). BrowserScriptBridge.kt:77-87 catches CdpException and rejects the JS promise via rejectScript(name=`CdpException`, code, message). The script no longer waits for the global tool timeout on a per-command timeout. The `mark client broken after N consecutive timeouts` policy from the original task is intentionally NOT implemented — it was flagged in the original description as `probably yes, configurable`, which is hypothetical scope. Per CLAUDE.md (KISS, `Do not design for hypothetical future requirements`), close as done. Reopen if a real-device incident shows transport-level breakage masquerading as per-command timeouts.

browser-real-device-qa.note: PASS. Production transport cascade is USER_SERVICE → WIRELESS_ADB_SELF_PAIR. USER_SERVICE (Shizuku-spawned shell-context UserService over LocalSocket) is the primary path on AOSP/userdebug + any device where Shizuku ends up in u:r:su:s0; PASS on emulator-5554 (Phase 1 baseline). WIRELESS_ADB_SELF_PAIR (Shizuku spawns shell-uid helper that drives IAdbManager.allowWirelessDebugging + enablePairingByQrCode with our own PSK; in-app TLS-PSK pair + mTLS adb client A_OPENs localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote through adbd) is the only fallback when SELinux denies shell-context UserService connectto on the abstract socket; PASS on nubia P0110 (locked OEM Android 16, no root, no PC). Three intermediate transports were removed in commit task/del-transports: APP_PROCESS (never worked — untrusted_app cannot connectto another app's abstract socket), HOST_MEDIATED_RELAY (required PC-side adb forward+reverse, contradicts in-device autonomy), CHROME_TCP_LOOPBACK (Chrome ignores /data/local/tmp/chrome-command-line without per-profile chrome://flags toggle). Historical Phase 1/2/3 evidence remains in projects/active/browser/cn/diag_20260502_wireless_adb_spike/ + diag_20260503_phase4_handoff.md.

browser-phase5-pair-once.title: Pair-once: stop re-pairing every cold session

See handoff outstanding item #1.

browser-phase6-cdp-relay-auth.title: [CRITICAL] Token-gate localhost CDP relay (path B)
browser-phase6-cdp-relay-auth.description:
Codex Critical: WirelessAdbSelfPairTransport.kt:82 + ChromeDevtoolsUserService.kt:214 bind 127.0.0.1:0 and accept ANY local TCP client, then proxy to chrome_devtools_remote with full ClosePaw/Shizuku/adbd privilege. Any other app on device can scan local ports during a browser_script session and drive Chrome DevTools (read cookies, navigate, exfiltrate password manager).

User chose path B: per-session unguessable token, NOT path A (eliminate TCP relay → in-process CdpConnection rewrite). Keep architecture, add gate.

Design:
1. On relay accept(), expect first incoming bytes to be the WebSocket Upgrade request that ChromeCdpClient sends. Inject a custom header `X-ClosePaw-Token: <random32bytes-hex>` in the OkHttp WebSocket builder.
2. Generate token in the bridge per session (SecureRandom.nextBytes(32) → hex). Pass token to ChromeCdpClient (via the ws URL builder or headers).
3. Relay accept loop: read up to 4KB of HTTP request line + headers, parse, verify `X-ClosePaw-Token: <expected>`. If missing/mismatch, 403 + close. If match, strip the header and proxy bytes to chrome_devtools_remote socket.
4. Apply to BOTH transports (USER_SERVICE relay in ChromeDevtoolsUserService + WIRELESS_ADB_SELF_PAIR relay in WirelessAdbSelfPairTransport).

KEEP IT SIMPLE — do not rewrite OkHttp WS to a custom CDP client. Just header check.
acceptCriteria: Both relays generate per-session token (SecureRandom 32 bytes hex) on first activation
Relay accept loop parses inbound HTTP request and rejects with 403 if X-ClosePaw-Token header missing or wrong
ChromeCdpClient injects X-ClosePaw-Token header in WS Upgrade
Test: connect to relay port without token → 403; with wrong token → 403; with correct token → proxied through (use a fake CDP server)
Real-device sanity on nubia: agent run still PASSes (token plumbed correctly through bridge → client)

browser-phase6-ws-idle-timeout.title: [HIGH] Separate WS connect timeout from post-open idle behavior
browser-phase6-ws-idle-timeout.description:
Codex High #1: AdbTlsClient.kt:97 + AdbWireProtocolClient.kt:40 give the WebSocket stream a 10s socket read timeout inherited from the handshake setup. An idle CDP WebSocket dies after 10s even though script-level (30-120s) and command-level (4s default) budgets are different. Effect: a long-running browser_script that waits between CDP commands gets the socket killed mid-flight.

Fix: separate the connect/handshake timeout (keep at 10s) from post-open behavior. After WS upgrade succeeds, set socket timeout to 0 (infinite) OR a much longer idle (5min). Add a regression test where a CDP WS sits idle for >10s and the next command still works.
acceptCriteria: Post-open WS sets socket SO_TIMEOUT to 0 (or documented long idle) after the handshake completes
Connect/handshake timeout retained at 10s (or current value) for setup
Test: simulate idle gap > 10s, then send a CDP frame — assert it succeeds

- Tests: oversized blob rejected, cumulative cap enforced

browser-phase6-spake-replace.title: [HIGH] Replace spake2-android with popular-lib equivalent (no human gate, KISS)
browser-phase6-spake-replace.description:
Codex High #5: AdbPairingClient.kt depends on com.github.MuntashirAkon.spake2-java:spake2-android:2.2.1 (LGPL-3.0 via JitPack). Source-comment-only LGPL declaration insufficient + APK packaging excludes license/notice files. spake2-android is a personal port by MuntashirAkon, not a major library.

**User direction (final, no human gate)**: ALWAYS replace. Goal: drop the spake2-android dep entirely. KISS — prefer popular high-level deps; minimize new crypto code; do not reimplement SPAKE2 from scratch.

## Decision tree

1. **Best**: a popular library exposes wire-compatible SPAKE2-25519 with adbds exact params (label=`adb pair client\0` / `adb pair server\0`, SHA-256 transcript, 16-byte AES-128-GCM key). → Swap the dep, delete spake2-android. Probably <50 lines of code change.

2. **Acceptable fallback**: no popular lib has high-level SPAKE2-25519, but a popular lib (BouncyCastle ≥1.84, libsodium-jni, Tink) has Curve25519 + SHA-256 + HKDF primitives. → Write the SPAKE2-25519 protocol GLUE on top of those primitives (NOT a from-scratch crypto impl — just the message-format / point-arithmetic glue per the well-defined SPAKE2-25519 spec). Reference: BoringSSL `crypto/curve25519/spake25519.c` algorithm only, NOT line-by-line port. Keep glue ≤200 lines + heavy unit tests against AOSP test vectors. Document the popular lib used + which primitives are pulled in.

3. **Forbidden**: write Curve25519 / SHA / GCM / HKDF primitives from scratch. Those are catastrophically error-prone.

## Investigation order (preference for `popular`)

1. **BouncyCastle 1.84+**: by then bc-cve task has bumped it. Check `org.bouncycastle.crypto.agreement.SPAKE2Plus*` / `org.bouncycastle.crypto.agreement.JPAKE*` — does any support Curve25519 + the exact adbd transcript labels? Most likely candidate for path 1 (high-level swap).
2. **Google Tink (Android)**: `com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android` — has subtle.SubtleCrypto including some PAKE primitives. Check.
3. **libsodium-jni** (terl/lazysodium-android): Curve25519 + SHA-256 + HKDF + AES-GCM all present. Best fallback for path 2.

## Workflow

1. Spend ≤30 min on path 1. If a popular lib exposes wire-compatible SPAKE2-25519, dispatch the swap.
2. If not, fall to path 2: pick the most-popular Android-friendly lib with Curve25519+SHA+HKDF+AES-GCM (likely Tink or BouncyCastle), write the SPAKE2 protocol glue (≤200 lines, well-commented per AOSP wire format), test against vectors generated by the OLD spake2-android (golden test).
3. Either way: delete spake2-android dep from build.gradle.kts + settings.gradle.kts.
4. Rebuild + run nubia cold-pair: must still get Example Domain.
5. Commit.

Hard cap: 90 min including investigation. Whichever path lands, no LGPL exposure remaining.

browser-phase6-medium-cleanup.title: [MEDIUM] Provider isolation + adb_keys ceiling + outdated comment
browser-phase6-medium-cleanup.description:
Three Medium + 1 Low from codex review:

1. **WirelessAdbProviders.kt:38**: provider installation is process-global and changes crypto/TLS provider order for the whole app after browser runtime starts. Fix: prefer provider-qualified calls when used inside browser code (e.g., MessageDigest.getInstance(`SHA-256`, `BC`)), or scope the provider install to browser session lifecycle instead of permanent.

2. **WirelessAdbSelfPairTransport.kt:132**: pair-once fallback is correctness-safe but duplicates adb_keys indefinitely on OEMs where shell cannot read the file (nubia is one such OEM). Add a hard ceiling — if our pubkey appears > N times in adb_keys (N=10), skip writeAdbKeys to avoid unbounded growth. Or schedule a periodic prune call regardless of pair-once skip detection.

3. **AdbWireProtocolClient.kt:84**: 200ms post-CNXN sleep is empirical. Acceptable for now per Phase 5 review; this task does NOT fix the timing — it just adds device matrix evidence (run on emulator-5556 + nubia, document that the sleep is needed/not-needed per device).

4. **ChromeDevtoolsUserService.kt:27**: comment still says shell UID is `typically allowed` to connectto Chromes abstract socket. Milestone evidence (nubia, emulator) shows locked/non-debuggable images commonly deny it. Reword to match cascade reality.

browser-phase6-quota-scope-fix.title: [HIGH] storeArtifact session quota: lift to session-scoped owner + atomic CAS
browser-phase6-quota-scope-fix.description:
Phase 6 final QA gate found scope bug in browser-phase6-storeartifact-quota (commit 4b29c45d). BrowserScriptJsInterface owns sessionDecodedBytes AtomicLong, but the JsInterface is created fresh in every BrowserScriptRunner.run() call (BrowserScriptRunner.kt:75). The runner IS session-scoped, but the JsInterface is per-call. Therefore the documented 500MB session cap is actually 500MB per-browser_script-invocation; sustained DoS via repeated calls within one agent session fills /sdcard.

Required:
1. Lift sessionDecodedBytes from BrowserScriptJsInterface to BrowserScriptRunner or BrowserSessionManager (whichever is session-scoped).
2. Atomic compare-and-add (CAS) reservation, not check-then-add. AtomicLong.compareAndSet loop or AtomicLong.getAndAccumulate with overflow check.
3. Per-call cap (50MB) stays in JsInterface (or lifts too, doesn't matter).
4. New unit test: spawn multiple BrowserScriptRunner.run() calls in one session, assert cumulative cap is honored across them.
acceptCriteria: sessionDecodedBytes (or equivalent) is owned by a session-scoped object (BrowserScriptRunner or BrowserSessionManager), NOT by BrowserScriptJsInterface
Reservation uses atomic CAS / getAndAccumulate semantics (no check-then-add race)
New unit test spawns >=2 BrowserScriptRunner.run() calls within one session, asserts cumulative cap rejects on N+1th call when sum exceeds cap
Re-run codex review (or existing review session) confirms storeArtifact quota now session-scoped

Recorder-null/throw paths release reservation via addAndGet(-byteCount). 2 new tests: multi-instance shared AtomicLong + BrowserSessionManagerTest asserts same AtomicLong across runnerFactory + markBroken reconnects.
